item.title: Arsenal star breaks silence on his future amid exit rumours
item.description: Arsenal star breaks silence on his future amid exit rumours Martin Odegaard Arsenal Future Clear as Captain Signals Long-Term Emirates Stay Martin Odegaard has addressed the noise around his Arsenal future and, for now, the message is simple. He wants to stay. There has been speculation because that is what happens when a key player moves into the final stretch of a contract cycle and carries a few injury concerns along the way. Yet the facts are straightforward. Odegaard remains central to Mikel Arteta’s midfield, remains club captain and remains productive for the Premier League champions. Odegaard contract situation remains calm The Norway international was asked directly about his plans and did not leave much room for interpretation. “I’m happy and hope I can stay there [at Arsenal] for a long time to come, but we haven’t started on that yet,” he replied to questions on his contract by Norwegian reporters. That is the update. No drama, no coded message, no public pressure. Just a player saying he is settled and open to staying in north London. His current Arsenal contract runs until June 2028, so there is time. Clubs prefer clarity, players prefer security, and these situations usually get sorted when it suits both sides. Photo: IMAGO Arsenal midfield competition has not shifted his role Arsenal have spent heavily in midfield and the competition has grown. Eberechi Eze, Mikel Merino and Bruno Guimaraes have all increased the depth around Arteta’s 4-3-3, but none of that has pushed Odegaard out of his place. He has kept his role in the advanced midfield slot because he still gives Arsenal control, movement and end product. He has featured in all 10 Premier League matches this season and scored three goals. That matters more than transfer gossip. Captain still delivering in key moments His latest contribution was decisive. Against Hull City, Arsenal were frustrated for 72 minutes before Odegaard reacted quickest to a rebound and scored the winner in a 1-0 victory. It was not glamorous, but it was valuable, and it moved Arsenal five points clear of Manchester City at the top. Next comes Newcastle United away under Matthias Jaissle, followed by Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League. Arsenal will want their captain fit, available and, if possible, talking less about contracts and more on the pitch.

item.description: The Minnesota Vikings started the 2026 season with an impressive performance but have been struggling offensively. The organization made one of the biggest moves of the season. The franchise required its former quarterback Kirk Cousins at Tuesday’s trade deadline. Cousins has been one of the major contributors to the organization and brought stability to Minnesota for years something that has been missing for fans and the players on the team since his departure in 2023. item.title: 49ers Rookie Called NFL’s Top ‘Breakout Candidate’
item.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling. Getty The San Francisco 49ers might have an ace in the hole for the stretch run of the regular season — and his name is De’Zhaun Stribling. Fox Sports NFL reporter Greg Auman put the rookie wide receiver and 2026 2nd-round pick at the top of his list of the NFL’s “Breakout Candidates” for the stretch run of the season, with the 49ers sitting at 7-1 headed into Sunday’s Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys, but Stribling is still not due back in the lineup for several weeks. “San Francisco has won despite a huge rash of injuries at receiver, and Stribling has been sidelined since he sprained his ankle in the season opener,” Auman wrote on November 13. “The 33rd overall pick this year out of Ole Miss had rave reviews in preseason, and if the 49ers are to make any kind of push in the playoffs, they’ll need a talented complement to Mike Evans. They got Keenan Allen at the trade deadline, but the 49ers probably need a little youth in that receiver room, too.” 49ers Give Injury Timeline Update on Stribling Stribling went from a highly questionable selection at No. 33 overall to earning a starting spot for the season opener against the Los Angeles Rams. Unfortunately for Stribling and the 49ers, he suffered a severe ankle injury in Week 1 that required surgery to repair the deltoid ligament — whatever that is — but it’s cost him almost his entire rookie season. The key word there: almost. The latest news on Stribling is good, and it appears he’s on track for a late-season return and could be an incredible weapon for the 49ers down the stretch. “One notable sight from the 49ers’ open locker room today: De’Zhaun Stribling walking around without crutches or any sort of brace/support on his lower leg,” The Athletic’s Matt Barrows wrote on X on November 3. “De’Zhaun Stribling likely won’t return to live reps until December (Week 13-15 range),” Dr. Jeff Mueller wrote on his official X account. “Great to hear he’s out of the boot + off crutches. Needs to ramp up agility, loading capacity, and sharp change of direction ability. A lot to do in the next 5-6 weeks.” Stribling’s Rare Combination of Size & Speed If Stribling is right, his combination of size and speed could take the offense to another level — he’s 6-foot-3, 206 pounds, and ran the 40-yard dash in a stunning 4.36 seconds at the NFL Scouting Combine. “Friendly reminder, De’Zhaun Stribling will return this season and the 49ers will be even more explosive on offense,” Coach Yac wrote on their official X account. Stribling, the No. 33 overall pick in the 2nd round, led the 49ers with 7 receptions for 63 yards in the preseason opener against the Tennessee Titans . He did so on just 8 targets, with all 7 receptions in the 1st half. item.title: Alabama expected to start Austin Mack at Vanderbilt as Keelon Russell deals with ankle injury
item.description: Austin Mack is expected to make the first start of his college career Saturday when the No. 3 Alabama Crimson Tide visit the Vanderbilt Commodores, ESPN’s Alex Scarborough reported Friday. Keelon Russell, who has started all nine games this season, hurt his ankle in the second half of Alabama’s 31-13 win at LSU on Nov. 7 and finished that game with the ankle wrapped. Russell is expected to be available off the bench, according to Scarborough, but the plan is to hold him out and give the injury time to heal. Kickoff at FirstBank Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee, is set for 12:45 p.m. ET on SEC Network. Alabama is resting a quarterback who has been one of the most productive in the country. Russell has completed 165 of 245 passes for 2,263 yards with 18 touchdowns and five interceptions, added 276 rushing yards and five more scores, and owns the second-best QBR in the nation behind Miami’s Darian Mensah. He spent two seasons behind Jalen Milroe and Ty Simpson, then entered 2026 in an open competition with Russell that ran through spring practice and into preseason camp. item.title: UCLA improves to 10-0 for the first time since 1998 with 22-14 win over Illinois
item.description: The No. 4 UCLA Bruins beat the Illinois Fighting Illini 22-14 on Friday night at the Rose Bowl, improving to 10-0 for the first time since 1998, the last season in which the program won a conference championship. It is the third 10-0 start in UCLA history, and it comes a year after the Bruins won three games, according to The Associated Press . UCLA (10-0, 7-0 Big Ten) is one of two unbeaten teams left in the country, along with No. 2 Utah, and it needs one more win to clinch a spot in the Big Ten championship game. Oct 17, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA Bruins head coach Bob Chesney in the first half against the Wisconsin Badgers at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Ty Dieffenbach completed 13 of 20 passes for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception. He threw a 54-yard touchdown to Aidan Mizell and a 26-yard score to Semaj Morgan, and UCLA led 10-0 at halftime. Dieffenbach left the game just before halftime with a left shoulder injury. He returned after the break and completed all five of his passes on his first drive back, finishing it with a touchdown. Illinois (6-4, 4-3 Big Ten) came to Pasadena on a four-game winning streak and got back into the game in the fourth quarter. Katin Houser converted a fourth down on the drive and then found Collin Dixon for a 7-yard touchdown with 7:14 left, cutting UCLA’s lead to 19-14. Safety Scooter Jackson ended the next threat. His second interception of the night, with 2:42 remaining, went 41 yards to the Illinois 19, and Mateen Bhaghani’s field goal pushed the lead to 22-14. Illinois got one more possession, and an incomplete pass with 43 seconds left sealed the win. The two takeaways gave UCLA 29 forced turnovers through 10 games. How UCLA got here Bob Chesney is in his first season as UCLA’s head coach after arriving from James Madison. The Bruins were eighth in the initial College Football Playoff rankings and moved up to fourth this week. Dieffenbach opened the season as a backup. He took over after starter Nico Iamaleava suffered a knee injury in UCLA’s Oct. 10 win at Oregon, and he is now 5-0 as a starter. His first start was a 17-7 win over Wisconsin in which he threw for 264 yards, and he was earned Big Ten player of the week honors after the win at Minnesota on Nov. 7, when he threw for a career-high 303 yards and three touchdowns on just eight completions. Oct 10, 2026; Eugene, Oregon, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) drops back for a pass during the first quarter against the Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images UCLA closes the regular season against Michigan and USC. A win in either game sends the Bruins to the Big Ten championship game in Indianapolis, where they would have a chance at the program’s first conference title since 1998. item.title: LSU’s Princewill Umanmielen fires back at Ole Miss with bold claims in $550,000 lawsuit
item.description: Princewill Umanmielen has responded to the lawsuit the Ole Miss Rebels filed against him in July, and his filing goes after two things: the circumstances in which he signed his 2026 revenue-sharing contract with the Rebels, and the county where the case is being heard. The LSU Tigers edge rusher argues he signed the agreement under “undue pressure” from Ole Miss coaches, according to the filing, which Jon Blau of The Advocate reported Friday . He also contends he cannot get a fair trial in Oxford, home of both the Ole Miss campus and the Lafayette County Circuit Court that is hearing the case. Oct 7, 2023; Columbia, Missouri, USA; A general view of a LSU Tigers helmet against the Missouri Tigers during the first half at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-USA TODAY Sports “Ole Miss has unclean hands and is entitled to no relief,” the filing reads. The venue request leans on the wording of Mississippi law, which lets a party move a civil case when the other side’s undue influence or prejudice in the public mind means he cannot receive a fair and impartial trial in the county where it is pending. Here, the party on the other side is the university whose main campus sits in that county. LSU’s Princewill Umanmielen is arguing he signed his 2026 rev share deal with Ole Miss under “undue pressure” from coaches. He also says he can’t get a fair trial in Oxford. “Ole Miss has unclean hands,” the filing reads, “and is entitled to no relief.” https://t.co/UkDGBCPG7Q — Jon Blau (@Jon_Blau) November 13, 2026 A contract signed between two playoff games Ole Miss sued Umanmielen and offensive lineman Devin Harper on July 27, seeking $550,000 from Umanmielen and $400,000 from Harper, plus attorneys’ fees and court costs. The school says a departure within the first 90 days of the agreement triggered an early-termination payment due within 30 days, and that neither player paid. Lane Kiffin left Ole Miss for LSU on Nov. 30, 2025, before the Rebels began their College Football Playoff run. Ole Miss’ timeline puts Umanmielen’s signature at 10:02 p.m. on Jan. 3, between the Rebels’ quarterfinal against the Georgia Bulldogs on Jan. 1 and their semifinal against the Miami Hurricanes on Jan. 8. He played in that Miami game, then left the program on Jan. 15, one day before the transfer portal closed, and followed Kiffin to Baton Rouge. Kiffin has declined to say if he knew about the players’ contracts and buyout terms when he recruited them. item.description: The Buffalo Bills move forward in the 2026 NFL season with a matchup against the New York Jets on the road with a 1 p.m. kickoff on Sunday from MetLife Stadium. CB Davison Igbinosun Igbinosun was tasked with covering All-Pro receiver Justin Jefferson last week after Christian Benford (wrist) went down with injury. DT Deone Walker The Jets have shown a commitment to running to ball but with a twist. Since Breece Hall returned from injury, New York's coaching staff has wanted to continue getting Braelon Allen involved as well. item.description: Report – Inter Closing In on Four Major Contract Renewals Inter are working to secure the futures of four key players, with Carlos Augusto and Hakan Calhanoglu expected to agree new contracts before Christmas. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the Nerazzurri have made progress in negotiations with the Brazilian defender and the Turkish midfielder. Meanwhile, they have also opened discussions with Marcus Thuram and Federico Dimarco. Carlos Augusto appears closest to putting pen to paper. The 27-year-old is reportedly on the verge of extending his stay at San Siro until 2031, with his annual salary set to rise to €3.5 million plus bonuses. His current deal runs until 2028. item.title: Forrest's stressful year ends with Christmas shopping in Augusta
item.description: Grant Forrest is nine shots behind leader Tyrrell Hatton going into the final round of the DP World Tour Championship [Getty Images] "It's a stressful way to do it, relying on one tournament a year." Grant Forrest admits his season "has not been a whole lot of fun", but what a week he chose to pull everything together. A Spanish Open triumph in October earned the 33-year-old Scot spots at The Masters and The Open Championship in 2027 while securing his future at the top level for at least two more years. It also secured a place at at this week's DP World Tour Championship in Dubai , with Forrest among the leading 50 players in the Tour rankings. A four-under-par back nine during his third round at Jumeirah Golf Estates moved him to level par and a share of 25th place. Prior to his terrific showing in Madrid, Forrest had four other top 20 finishes in 2026, along with nine missed cuts. "It's been very similar to last season," he said. "Bar one tournament, it's not been a whole lot of fun, to be honest. "But if you said to anyone you were going to play poorly but win an event every season for your career, you'd bite their hand off." Looking ahead to his Masters debut, Forrest revealed he will get some practice at the iconic Augusta National in December after being invited to play by contacts who know members at the club. He first visited Augusta as a spectator in 2019 and recognises that experiencing the course as a player will be an entirely different proposition. "One of the guys I know from home knows a few members, so we're kindly being hosted just the week before Christmas," he said. "The more times you've played it going out before April, the better, and that's exciting." Asked if he would be taking advantage of the opportunity to visit the famous merchandise shop, Forrest added: "I'll be taking an empty suitcase and picking up a few Christmas presents."

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results, kick-off times and how to watch
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. South Africa and New Zealand are assured of a top-two finish in their pool – with the All Blacks given a huge opportunity to seize the initiative after the Springboks were beaten by France. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. item.title: How FSU football's 'simplified' defense sparked road win vs. Pitt
item.description: Florida State football needed a refresh. Mike Norvell's tenure had run its course in Tallahassee, and after the Seminoles ' loss to Clemson on Halloween, the university decided it was time to part ways after seven seasons. Out went Norvell, alongside defensive coordinator Tony White and safeties coach Evan Cooper. It thrust Rick Stockstill, interim head coach, and Ernie Sims, interim defensive coordinator, into new roles. They had four games to help the program avoid a third consecutive losing season. Since? FSU has rattled off a pair of wins on the road — the first time the Seminoles have done so since 2023 — capped by a dominant defensive performance in a 16-10 win over Pitt. It was the final road game of the season, and one in which the Seminoles were considered underdogs, as the Panthers were 3.5-point favorites before kickoff, making this a sod game for FSU. "These last two weeks, we've done something that probably nobody thought we could do. I mean, we hadn't won a game on the road in two and a half years, and now we've gone back-to-back," Stockstill told reporters after the win on Friday, Nov. 13. "We were underdogs coming here, and we found a way to win." The midseason turnaround has put FSU on the verge of qualifying for a bowl game for the first time since 2023, and the Seminoles are back to .500 after the win at Pitt. They sit at 5-5 (3-4 ACC) with two games to play, both at Doak Campbell Stadium. While FSU's offense has produced some big moments, the defensive turnaround under Sims has been the catalyst for the late-season resurgence. Stockstill said he and Sims simplified the defense, transitioning away from White's 3-3-5 and into more four-down lineman looks. He felt that it took some stress off the players, particularly one group: the secondary. Against the Panthers, FSU deflected six passes, two of which came from Charles Lester III, and the defense recorded an interception, though it came from defensive lineman Rylan Kennedy rather than the secondary. "When you run a three-man front, there's so many different things that the secondary has to be responsible for in the run game as well as in the passing game. And we felt that we were putting too much pressure on them, just that they couldn't play. And you look at our corners now, man, we challenged a lot of balls out there," Stockstill said. "Four, Charles Lester, came in there and made some really nice plays. Ja'bril [Rawls], you know, six, he made some nice plays. 11 (CJ Richard Jr.) should have almost had that interception, you know. We're playing better and more consistently in the secondary, where we're not giving up big plays like we were previously. So, I think we've simplified things, and it's made everybody, not just the front but the back guys on the back end, more confident." item.description: What have your impressions been of Zuffa Boxing as a promoter in their first year of operations? Scott Christ You ever watch the show “Justified”? Without getting into spoilers, the series occasionally portrays instances of criminal forces from The Big City coming down to the Kentucky hill country with their eye on sort of, like, modernizing the drug empires of the region and whatnot. They have their money, their appearances, their belief that these hicks and rubes will be convinced to fall in line and they will take over the region, gloss it up and either chase off the rabble or bend the rabble to its will. I’ll leave it to you to either watch the show or take a guess as to how it tends to turn out when an invading element comes into not just someone else’s turf, but what really is exceptionally specialized turf that takes more than brute force to take and control. I never really thought Dana White would actually get into boxing. I had reasons for this. (1) He was busy with UFC, over which he was unquestioned ruler. (2) A promoter like him really needs to be unquestioned ruler. (3) He’d repeatedly “investigated” the idea and come to the conclusion that boxing was unfixable, at least if the gamble was going to actually have to be his. White is a figurehead. He didn’t have a “eureka!” moment and figure out a novel approach to boxing. The idea has been to gut legislation and have the opportunity and ability to turn boxing into something more akin to UFC. And the money was available for Zuffa Boxing to give it a go, to try and expand the monopolizing instincts that have boosted TKO’s other, already-proven businesses into the boxing world. The legislation has been in progress. But without the immediate, earthshaking changes to boxing’s foundations, Zuffa has operated like many previous — and ultimately failed, usually quickly — boxing promotional ventures, splashing money around seemingly without a clue on doomed-to-tank ideas that any established promoter would have told you was a shockingly, comically bad idea, like giving Conor Benn all that money. item.title: Tyler Adjei: Fabrizio Romano confirms United have completed deal to sign striker for academy
item.description: Tyler Adjei: Fabrizio Romano confirms United have completed deal to sign striker for academy Manchester United are entering another new era, having replaced Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino. Pochettino left the USMNT to manage United, a club he had apparently been hoping to lead since his time at Tottenham Hotspur. The Argentinian tactician has made his name with his high-intensity, attacking style of football. He also earned praise for developing young players in north London. Manchester United land Tyler Adjei Mauricio Pochettino gave more debuts (12) to players aged 21 or under than any other Premier League manager during his time at Tottenham Hotspur. As such, the Argentine may relish the opportunity to work with Manchester United’s academy, as INEOS have invested heavily in it over the last two years. They have also snapped up another exciting talent in recent days. According to Fabrizio Romano , Manchester United have completed a deal to sign Tyler Adjei from Reading. The Italian journalist posted an edited image of the youngster in a United shirt with his trademark statement, “Here We Go”, on it. “All done for 16-year-old to join #mufc project,” his post read. “Talented forward has accepted all terms, deal in place.” “Documents to be approved next week,” he added. Who is Tyler Adjei? Adjei is the first signing of the Mauricio Pochettino era, but he will initially be part of United’s under-18s, managed by Darren Fletcher . Born in England, Adjei is of Ghanaian descent. The highly-rated England youth international is primarily a number nine, but he can operate anywhere across the front three. He moves to United after making 19 appearances for Reading’s under-18s, scoring five goals in the process. “He’s got an athletic profile; he’s got more to come physically,” a source told The Athletic . “He moves well; he has a good temperament, mentality and demeanour. He has a good energy to train. He’s got a way to go technically, as is the norm for a player of his age.” According to Roundtable , the Red Devils beat three other English clubs, including Liverpool, to win the race for Adjei’s signature.

item.description: The Pittsburgh Penguins (7-10-2, 16 points) will look to build on their winning 2-1 California road trip Saturday when they take on the Ottawa Senators (12-6-2, 26 points) at home. On Wednesday, the Penguins capped off the three-game swing with a 3-2 shootout win over the San Jose Sharks . A 34-save effort by rookie goaltender Sergei Murashov led the way, and it was his second win of the road trip as well as the second-most saves he made in a game this season, the most being when he stole the Penguins a point against the Columbus Blue Jackets on Oct. 9 with 45 saves on 47 attempts. Even though a lot of the on-ice play was still a mixed bag for Pittsburgh - and their goaltender was outstanding enough to steal them a game yet again on Wednesday - they are some things to build off of. Their lineup seems to be gaining momentum, they are now near the top of the league in defensive zone giveaways with the third-fewest at 107, and they are actually beginning to see some synergy in their lineup. The advanced stats back up the Penguins playing better five-on-five hockey as of late, too. They are fourth in the league in expected goals for per 60 with 2.88, their PDO is seventh-lowest in the league this season at 97.79 to indicate some poor luck, and their Corsi (shot attempts share) is eighth in the league at 52.67 percent amongst a bunch of playoff-positioned teams. And injured defenseman Trevor van Riemsdyk did skate with the team Friday, but he was on the fourth pairing with Ilya Solovyov, perhaps an indication that he will not be in the lineup Saturday. item.title: Eugenio Chacarra comments on his chances of winning the Race to Dubai after Rory McIlroy’s poor third round
item.description: Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Eugenio Chacarra is currently sitting in a tie for fourth alongside Rory McIlroy with just one round remaining in Dubai. Chacarra posted a third round score of 68 on Saturday at the DP World Tour Championship, while McIlroy labored to a very ordinary 72. For golf fans watching at home, things could not be set up more perfectly heading into the final round on Sunday. Chacarra knows that he only has to finish ahead of McIlroy and Jon Rahm in order to clinch the season-long Race to Dubai title. Meanwhile, the Northern Irishman has to finish higher than the Spaniard, and no worse than fourth outright. There is obviously a lot of golf left to be played, and McIlroy will undoubtedly still be very confident in his chances of winning the Race to Dubai, especially given the experience he has. However, Chacarra is certainly not short of confidence either, and on Saturday afternoon, he spoke about his hopes of being crowned the season-long champion. Eugenio Chacarra on his chances of beating Rory McIlroy to the Race to Dubai title Chacarra spoke to reporters after his third round in Dubai on Saturday, and he was asked how he feels about his chances of winning the Race to Dubai on Sunday. “ Yeah, I mean, I just want to win the tournament. I’m not far away. I think I’m three shots out now. Hopefully they don’t make a lot of birdies coming in and I have a shot tomorrow. I know if I win the tournament, I win the ranking, “ the Spaniard replied. “ So that’s what I wanted to do in Abu Dhabi and I want to do it here. That’s what we prepare for and I’m going to have a chance on Sunday. That’s what we dream of since I was little is to win big events on Sunday, and I’m going to have a chance. “ I’m ready. I love the game of golf. I love practising. I work so hard for these moments, and I’m going to go out there and enjoy it. “ I think all of my goals have been done this season. So I’m just playing free. This is an extra bonus to have a chance to win it, and just to enjoy every moment. Like you said, not a lot of people can enjoy this moment and have a chance to win The Race to Dubai. So I’m going to have a chance tomorrow, and I’m going to go try and enjoy it as much as possible. “ All that remains to be seen now is whether Eugenio Chacarra is able to hold off Rory McIlroy on Sunday in order to win his first ever Race to Dubai crown.
